authority: the pooled DLD_RESULT.json combines z0 (well-powered, n=20 both arms) and z1 (underpowered, n=6 mismatch) into single aggregate statistics. DLD_POWER_RESOLUTION_AMENDMENT.json requires z0 and z1 be read separately. This computes and freezes that split from dld_branch_rows.csv.
amends: DLD_RESULT.json -- adds the by-latent split its own aggregate did not report; no number in DLD_RESULT.json is changed

Z0_WELL_POWERED_n20_BOTH_ARMS.reading: the mismatch arm is LESS volatile than the decision-sensitivity reference (0.100 vs 0.450), the reverse of what the leverage hypothesis predicted. 18 of 20 teacher-substitution branches produced the IDENTICAL final outcome to the student's own action. This is not a subtle statistical call: a null result (zero difference) is not confounded by the teacher-vs-runner-up quality asymmetry the way a positive leverage finding would have been, since zero is zero regardless of the counterfactual's quality.
Z0_WELL_POWERED_n20_BOTH_ARMS.licensed_conclusion_for_z0: per DECISION_LEVERAGE_DIAGNOSTIC_SPEC.json#PREREGISTERED_READINGS row 2 (leverage near zero / no larger than the reference): decision leverage is NOT the explanation for z0's crossover shortfall. Combined with covariate shift already refuted (ONPOLICY_TD_FALSIFICATION_SCOPE_AMENDMENT.json, DLD_TEACHER_MATCHING_CLARIFICATION_AMENDMENT.json) and macro imitation error already shown to be tiny (1.0-1.2%), the parameter-sharing architecture becomes the strongest remaining candidate FOR Z0 SPECIFICALLY.

Z1_UNDERPOWERED_n6_mismatch.reading: NO CONCLUSION drawn, per DLD_POWER_RESOLUTION_AMENDMENT.json. 6 points cannot support a leverage claim in either direction. This is unresolvable by DLD as designed: z1 has only 7 macro mismatches in its ENTIRE recorded dataset (DLD_PASS1_RECORD_V2.json), so no re-sampling or re-running of this diagnostic on this checkpoint can increase z1's power -- there is nothing more to sample.
Z1_UNDERPOWERED_n6_mismatch.the_open_anomaly: z1 reproduces pi_B's macro commitments at ~99.8% fidelity in both deployment conditions (DLD_PASS1_RECORD_V2.json), yet the sealed Compression Crossover measured V(z1,B)=0.4688 against specialist pi_B's own 0.625 on that pole (different blocks; descriptive). Whatever costs z1 its margin is, by construction, NOT a macro decision -- there are almost no macro decisions to blame, and DLD (a macro-level diagnostic) cannot see below that level.

NEXT_STEP_IMPLICATIONS.for_z0: the sharing-ladder architecture question is now the best-supported successor: covariate shift refuted, imitation error tiny, decision leverage refuted (reverse direction, cleanly). Two complete actors selected by z, progressively sharing more, would locate where z0's crossover margin is actually lost.
NEXT_STEP_IMPLICATIONS.for_z1: a DIFFERENT diagnostic is needed, not more DLD branching on this checkpoint: something that operates below the macro level (target-head selection, continuous/positional action detail, or a representational probe), since the mechanism cannot be a macro decision. This would be a fresh preregistered diagnostic, not a rescue of DLD.
